name: New York City
tagline: Skyline, museums and food from everywhere
summary: Plan Manhattan by neighbourhood: Lower Manhattan and the harbour, Midtown's towers, then Central Park and the museums. Walk a lot, take the subway for the rest, and cross to Brooklyn at least once.
seasonNote: July and August are hot and humid; December is festive and very expensive; January to March is cold and cheapest.
arrival: From JFK take the AirTrain and subway or LIRR (about an hour); Newark has a rail link; LaGuardia has buses and taxis.
gettingAround: Tap a contactless card on subways and buses; fares cap weekly. Walking is often fastest in Midtown.
cashTip: Cards work everywhere; tip 18 to 20% in restaurants and a dollar or two per drink.
foodTip: Have a bagel with lox, a slice of pizza, pastrami on rye, and dumplings in Chinatown or Flushing.
buyTip: Books, museum shop design pieces and sample-sale fashion.
baseArea: Midtown for first visits; the Lower East Side, Chelsea or Williamsburg for atmosphere

items.name: Central Park
items.summary: An 843-acre park of lawns, lakes and woodland in the middle of Manhattan.
items.expect: Bigger than it looks; cyclists on the loop road.
items.tip: Enter at 72nd Street for Bethesda Terrace, Bow Bridge and the Ramble.
items.why: It is the city's shared back garden and a design masterpiece.
flow: Walk The Mall to Bethesda Terrace.
Cross Bow Bridge and loop back by Strawberry Fields.

items.name: Metropolitan Museum of Art
items.summary: One of the world's largest art museums, from an Egyptian temple to modern painting.
items.expect: Far too big for one visit.
items.tip: Pick three sections; the roof garden is open in warm months.
items.why: It covers 5,000 years of art under one roof.
flow: See the Temple of Dendur and the Egyptian wing.
Then European paintings and the American Wing courtyard.

items.name: Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island
items.summary: Ferries to Liberty Island and the immigration museum on Ellis Island.
items.expect: Airport-style security; crown and pedestal tickets sell out months ahead.
items.tip: Book the first ferry with the official operator only; ignore street sellers.
items.why: The statue and Ellis Island tell the story of American immigration.
flow: First ferry from Battery Park.
Liberty Island, then Ellis Island.

items.name: Brooklyn Bridge and DUMBO
items.summary: A walk across the 1883 suspension bridge to cobbled waterfront streets with skyline views.
items.expect: Crowded at midday.
items.tip: Walk from Brooklyn towards Manhattan for the skyline ahead of you, at sunrise or dusk.
items.why: The best free view in New York.
flow: Subway to High Street, Brooklyn.
See Washington Street and the waterfront park, then walk across.

items.name: 9/11 Memorial and Museum
items.summary: Twin reflecting pools in the towers' footprints, with an underground museum.
items.expect: The memorial is free; the museum is ticketed and emotionally heavy.
items.tip: Allow two hours for the museum and book a timed ticket.
items.why: A powerful, carefully made memorial.
flow: Walk around both pools.
Go down into the museum.

items.name: The High Line and Chelsea Market
items.summary: A park on a disused elevated railway, running through galleries and new architecture.
items.expect: Slow-moving crowds at weekends.
items.tip: Walk north to south and finish with food at Chelsea Market.
items.why: A model for urban parks around the world.
flow: Start at Hudson Yards.
Walk to Gansevoort Street; detour into Chelsea Market.

items.name: Top of the Rock
items.summary: Open-air observation decks on the 70th floor of Rockefeller Center.
items.expect: Timed tickets; sunset slots cost extra and sell out.
items.tip: Choose this deck to see both the Empire State Building and Central Park.
items.why: The best-balanced skyline view in Midtown.
flow: Go up 45 minutes before sunset.
Stay for the lights.

items.name: Katz's Delicatessen
items.summary: A delicatessen from 1888 serving hand-carved pastrami on rye.
items.expect: Queues, and a ticket you must keep to pay on the way out.
items.tip: Go to a carver's line, tip a dollar and share one sandwich.
items.why: The definitive New York pastrami sandwich.
flow: Take a ticket at the door.
Order at a carving station and find a table.

items.name: Joe's Pizza
items.summary: A slice shop on Carmine Street since 1975.
items.expect: A queue and standing room.
items.tip: Order a plain cheese slice and eat it folded.
items.why: The standard for a classic New York slice.
flow: Queue at the counter.
Eat standing or in the nearby square.

items.name: Russ & Daughters
items.summary: A century-old 'appetizing' shop for smoked fish, bagels and cream cheese.
items.expect: Take a number; takeaway only at the shop.
items.tip: Go on a weekday morning; the café on Orchard Street has tables.
items.why: The best bagel and lox in the city.
flow: Take a number.
Order a bagel with Gaspe Nova and scallion cream cheese.

items.name: Chinatown dumplings
items.summary: Small shops around Mott, Doyers and Eldridge streets selling dumplings, noodles and roast meats.
items.expect: Some places are cash only.
items.tip: Eat at two or three shops rather than one.
items.why: Some of the best cheap food in Manhattan.
flow: Start on Doyers Street.
Try soup dumplings, then hand-pulled noodles.

name: San Francisco
tagline: Fog, hills and a red bridge
summary: A compact city of distinct neighbourhoods on steep hills. See the bridge and Alcatraz, eat in the Mission and Chinatown, and bring layers: summer is cold.
seasonNote: June to August is foggy and chilly; September and October are the warmest, clearest months.
arrival: BART trains run from SFO to downtown in about 30 minutes.
gettingAround: Use Muni buses, streetcars and cable cars with a contactless card; hills make walking slower than maps suggest.
cashTip: Cards work everywhere; tip 18 to 20% in restaurants.
foodTip: Try a Mission burrito, sourdough, Dungeness crab in season, dim sum and cioppino.
buyTip: Books from City Lights, Ghirardelli or small-batch chocolate, local sourdough.
baseArea: Union Square for transit; North Beach or Hayes Valley for character

items.name: Golden Gate Bridge
items.summary: The 1937 suspension bridge across the mouth of the bay.
items.expect: Often in fog on summer mornings; windy and cold on the span.
items.tip: Walk part-way from the Welcome Center, or cycle across to Sausalito and ferry back.
items.why: The most recognisable bridge in the world.
flow: Start at the south-side plaza.
Walk to the first tower, or cross fully.

items.name: Alcatraz Island
items.summary: The former federal prison on an island, visited with an excellent cellhouse audio tour.
items.expect: Tickets sell out weeks ahead in summer.
items.tip: Book with the official ferry operator from Pier 33; the night tour is the best.
items.why: The audio tour, narrated by former guards and inmates, is superb.
flow: Ferry from Pier 33.
Do the cellhouse audio tour, then walk the grounds.

items.name: Cable cars and Lombard Street
items.summary: A ride on the hand-operated cable cars over the hills, past the crooked block of Lombard Street.
items.expect: Long queues at the Powell Street turnaround.
items.tip: Board a few stops up the line, or ride the quieter California Street line.
items.why: The last manually operated cable car system in the world.
flow: Take the Powell-Hyde line.
Get off at Lombard Street and walk down.

items.name: Chinatown and North Beach
items.summary: The oldest Chinatown in North America, next to the Italian cafés and Beat-era bookshop of North Beach.
items.expect: Grant Avenue is for tourists; Stockton Street is where locals shop.
items.tip: Walk Stockton Street's markets, then cut to City Lights bookshop.
items.why: Two of the city's most characterful neighbourhoods back to back.
flow: Enter by the Dragon Gate.
Walk to Columbus Avenue and Washington Square.

items.name: Ferry Building and Embarcadero
items.summary: An 1898 ferry terminal turned food hall, with a farmers' market outside.
items.expect: The big market runs on Saturday mornings.
items.tip: Come on Saturday for the farmers' market.
items.why: The best showcase of Northern California produce.
flow: Walk the food hall.
Follow the waterfront towards Pier 39's sea lions.

items.name: Painted Ladies and Alamo Square
items.summary: A row of pastel Victorian houses with the downtown skyline behind.
items.expect: A quick photo stop on a sloping park.
items.tip: Afternoon light falls on the house fronts.
items.why: The city's classic postcard view.
flow: Climb the park slope.
Photograph the row with the skyline.

items.name: Muir Woods
items.summary: A valley of old-growth coast redwoods 40 minutes north of the bridge.
items.expect: Parking or shuttle reservations are required.
items.tip: Reserve parking or the shuttle in advance and arrive early.
items.why: The closest place to stand among giant redwoods.
flow: Drive or shuttle from Sausalito.
Walk the boardwalk loop to Cathedral Grove.

items.name: Tartine Bakery
items.summary: A bakery famous across the US for country bread and morning buns.
items.expect: A queue most mornings.
items.tip: Take pastries to Dolores Park two blocks away.
items.why: One of America's most influential bakeries.
flow: Queue at the counter.
Order a morning bun and a croissant.

items.name: La Taqueria
items.summary: A Mission taqueria known for rice-free burritos and crisp tacos.
items.expect: A queue, shared tables and cash preferred.
items.tip: Ask for it 'dorado' to have the burrito griddled.
items.why: Often named the best burrito in America.
flow: Order at the counter.
Wait for your number.

items.name: Swan Oyster Depot
items.summary: An 18-stool seafood counter open since 1912.
items.expect: Waits of an hour or more; cash only; closes mid-afternoon.
items.tip: Arrive before opening on a weekday.
items.why: A San Francisco institution for oysters and crab.
flow: Queue outside.
Order a combination salad, oysters and chowder.

name: Vancouver
tagline: A city between ocean and mountains
summary: Cycle the seawall, eat at Granville Island and spend a day in the North Shore mountains. The city is compact and outdoor life is the main attraction.
seasonNote: October to March is rainy; summer is dry, sunny and the peak for cruises.
arrival: The Canada Line SkyTrain reaches downtown from the airport in 25 minutes.
gettingAround: Walk, cycle or use SkyTrain, buses and the SeaBus with a contactless card.
cashTip: Cards work everywhere; tip 15 to 20% in restaurants.
foodTip: Try sushi, wild salmon, dim sum in Richmond and a Japadog.
buyTip: Indigenous art from galleries that name the artist, maple syrup and smoked salmon.
baseArea: Downtown, the West End or Yaletown

connections.note: About 9 hours' drive; or fly to Calgary and drive 90 minutes.

items.name: Stanley Park Seawall
items.summary: A 9 km waterfront path around a forested peninsula, passing totem poles and beaches.
items.expect: The cycling lane is one-way, anticlockwise.
items.tip: Rent a bike on Denman Street and allow 90 minutes with stops.
items.why: The best way to see the city, mountains and harbour together.
flow: Rent a bike near the park entrance.
Stop at the totem poles and Prospect Point.

items.name: Granville Island
items.summary: A former industrial site of artisan studios, theatres and a large public market.
items.expect: Very busy at weekends.
items.tip: Arrive by the small Aquabus ferry.
items.why: The city's favourite food and craft stop.
flow: Take the mini-ferry across False Creek.
Explore the market and the studios.

items.name: Capilano Suspension Bridge Park
items.summary: A 137-metre footbridge swaying 70 metres above a river, with treetop and cliff walkways.
items.expect: Expensive and crowded; free shuttle from downtown.
items.tip: Go at opening; Lynn Canyon is a free, smaller alternative.
items.why: A dramatic way into the coastal rainforest.
flow: Shuttle from Canada Place.
Cross the bridge and walk the Treetops Adventure.

items.name: Grouse Mountain
items.summary: A gondola to a mountaintop with city views, grizzly bears in a refuge and winter skiing.
items.expect: Pointless in low cloud; check the webcam.
items.tip: Fit hikers can climb the steep Grouse Grind and ride down.
items.why: The classic view over Vancouver.
flow: Ride the Skyride.
See the bear habitat and viewpoints.

items.name: Gastown
items.summary: The city's oldest neighbourhood: cobbles, Victorian warehouses and a steam-powered clock.
items.expect: It borders the troubled Downtown Eastside; stay on the main streets.
items.tip: Catch the steam clock on the quarter hour.
items.why: Where Vancouver began, now full of design shops and bars.
flow: Walk Water Street.
Stop at the steam clock and Maple Tree Square.

items.name: Museum of Anthropology
items.summary: A glass-and-concrete museum of Northwest Coast First Nations art and totem poles.
items.expect: A 30-minute bus ride from downtown; closed on Mondays in winter.
items.tip: Join a free gallery tour.
items.why: The best place to understand the region's Indigenous cultures.
flow: See the Great Hall of totem poles.
Find Bill Reid's 'The Raven and the First Men'.

items.name: Granville Island Public Market
items.summary: A covered market of produce, bakeries, smoked salmon and food counters.
items.expect: Seats are scarce and seagulls bold.
items.tip: Assemble a picnic and eat on the dock.
items.why: The best lunch stop in the city.
flow: Do a lap of the stalls.
Buy doughnuts, salmon and a pie.

items.name: Miku
items.summary: A waterfront restaurant that popularised flame-seared aburi sushi in Canada.
items.expect: Book ahead for dinner.
items.tip: Lunch sets are good value.
items.why: Its seared salmon oshi sushi is a Vancouver signature.
flow: Reserve a table.
Order the salmon oshi and a premium sushi selection.

items.name: Japadog
items.summary: A street cart turned local chain selling hot dogs with Japanese toppings.
items.expect: A short queue.
items.tip: Try the Terimayo with seaweed and teriyaki sauce.
items.why: A cheap, only-in-Vancouver snack.
flow: Order at the cart or shop.
Eat on the go.

name: Banff
tagline: Turquoise lakes in the Canadian Rockies
summary: Base in Banff town for the lakes and peaks of Canada's first national park. Lake Louise and Moraine Lake need shuttle bookings; the Icefields Parkway is a full-day drive.
seasonNote: Lakes thaw in June; Moraine Lake's road is open roughly June to mid-October. December to March is ski season.
arrival: Fly to Calgary; airport shuttles and the drive take about 90 minutes.
gettingAround: Roam buses cover the town and Lake Louise; a car is best for the Icefields Parkway.
cashTip: Cards work everywhere; a national park pass is needed per day.
foodTip: Try Alberta beef, bison, a Caesar cocktail and a BeaverTail pastry.
buyTip: Outdoor gear, maple products and local art.
via: Fly into Calgary, then about 90 minutes by road

connections.note: About 9 hours' drive, or fly from Calgary.

costNote: Park pass, shuttles and gondolas are extra.

items.name: Lake Louise
items.summary: A turquoise glacial lake beneath Victoria Glacier.
items.expect: Parking is full by sunrise in summer.
items.tip: Book the Parks Canada shuttle and walk to the Lake Agnes Tea House.
items.why: The most famous view in the Rockies.
flow: Shuttle from the Park and Ride.
Walk the lakeshore, then hike to Lake Agnes.

items.name: Moraine Lake
items.summary: A vivid blue lake ringed by ten peaks.
items.expect: No private cars; shuttle or tour bus only, and it is closed in winter.
items.tip: Book the shuttle the moment reservations open; climb the Rockpile for the view.
items.why: Many find it even more beautiful than Lake Louise.
flow: Take the shuttle from the Park and Ride.
Climb the Rockpile, then walk the shore.
items.best: Sunrise or morning, June to early October

items.name: Banff Gondola and Sulphur Mountain
items.summary: A gondola to a 2,281-metre summit with a ridge boardwalk and views of six ranges.
items.expect: Pricey; cheaper off-peak slots.
items.tip: Hike up for free and ride down, or go late for sunset.
items.why: The best panorama near town.
flow: Ride the gondola.
Walk the boardwalk to Sanson's Peak.

items.name: Johnston Canyon
items.summary: Catwalks bolted to canyon walls lead to two waterfalls.
items.expect: Very busy at midday; icy in winter.
items.tip: Go before 9 am or after 5 pm.
items.why: The most accessible canyon walk in the park.
flow: Walk to the Lower Falls.
Continue to the Upper Falls.

items.name: Icefields Parkway
items.summary: A 230 km mountain highway past glaciers, Peyto Lake and the Columbia Icefield.
items.expect: No phone signal and one fuel stop; a full day.
items.tip: Drive as far as the Columbia Icefield and back, stopping at Bow and Peyto lakes.
items.why: One of the world's great scenic drives.
flow: Start early from Lake Louise.
Stop at Bow Lake, Peyto Lake and the Athabasca Glacier.

items.name: Banff Upper Hot Springs
items.summary: An outdoor thermal pool with mountain views.
items.expect: A public pool, busy in the evening.
items.tip: Go after a hike or on a snowy evening.
items.why: The hot springs are the reason the park was founded.
flow: Rent a towel and locker.
Soak with a view of Mount Rundle.

items.name: Park Distillery
items.summary: A restaurant and distillery serving campfire-style cooking.
items.expect: Busy; book for dinner.
items.tip: Try a spirit flight made with glacier water.
items.why: The town's most distinctive place to eat.
flow: Reserve a table.
Order rotisserie chicken or bison.

items.name: Lake Agnes Tea House
items.summary: A log tea house from 1905 beside a mountain lake, reached only on foot.
items.expect: A 3.5 km uphill hike; cash preferred; open June to early October.
items.tip: Start by 8 am to get a table.
items.why: Tea and fresh bread taste better after the climb.
flow: Hike up from Lake Louise.
Order tea and a sandwich on the porch.

items.name: BeaverTails
items.summary: A stand selling flat fried dough pastries with sweet toppings.
items.expect: A queue on summer evenings.
items.tip: The classic is cinnamon sugar with lemon.
items.why: A Canadian treat for a walk along Banff Avenue.
flow: Order at the window.
Eat it warm.

name: Victoria Falls
summary: A small town built around the world's largest sheet of falling water. Two or three days cover the falls, a Zambezi sunset cruise and a day safari in Chobe.
seasonNote: Water peaks March to May (wet, misty views); by October and November the Zambian side can be dry.
arrival: Victoria Falls airport is 20 minutes from town; a KAZA Univisa covers Zimbabwe and Zambia.
gettingAround: The town is walkable by day; use hotel shuttles or taxis after dark because of wildlife.
cashTip: US dollars in small notes are the working currency; cards work at hotels and larger restaurants.
foodTip: Try sadza with stew, Zambezi bream and game meats such as kudu.
buyTip: Shona stone sculpture and carvings from the craft market; bargain politely.
baseArea: Victoria Falls town, within walking distance of the park
via: Usually via Johannesburg, Addis Ababa or Nairobi

connections.note: Direct flights on some days; otherwise via Johannesburg.

costNote: Park entry is about USD 50 and activities are priced in US dollars.

items.name: Victoria Falls rainforest walk
items.summary: A path along the gorge rim opposite the 1.7 km-wide curtain of falling water.
items.expect: You will be soaked at high water; viewpoints are slippery.
items.tip: Bring a raincoat and a waterproof phone pouch; go at opening or late afternoon for rainbows.
items.why: It is one of the natural wonders of the world.
flow: Start at the Livingstone statue and Devil's Cataract.
Walk the 16 viewpoints to Danger Point.

items.name: Zambezi sunset cruise
items.summary: A two-hour boat trip above the falls, with drinks, hippos, crocodiles and sometimes elephants.
items.expect: Boats range from large and lively to small and quiet.
items.tip: Pay a little more for a smaller boat.
items.why: The classic way to end a day at the falls.
flow: Hotel pick-up around 4 pm.
Cruise the river islands until sunset.

items.name: Victoria Falls Bridge
items.summary: A 1905 steel arch bridge over the gorge, with a bungy jump, swing and guided walk beneath it.
items.expect: You need your passport and a free bridge pass at the border post.
items.tip: Walk out for the view even if you don't jump.
items.why: A feat of engineering, with a view of the falls from the middle.
flow: Get a bridge pass at Zimbabwean immigration.
Walk to the middle of the span.

items.name: Chobe National Park day trip
items.summary: A day across the border in Botswana, with a river safari by boat and a game drive.
items.expect: A long day with a border crossing; check visa needs.
items.tip: Dry season (June to October) brings huge elephant herds to the river.
items.why: Chobe has one of Africa's largest elephant populations.
flow: Transfer about 75 minutes to Kasane.
Morning boat safari, lunch, afternoon game drive.

items.name: Devil's Pool
items.summary: A natural rock pool on the very lip of the falls, reached by boat and a guided swim.
items.expect: Only at low water (about late August to December), on the Zambian side.
items.tip: Book well ahead and bring your passport for the border.
items.why: You look straight over a 100-metre drop.
flow: Cross to Zambia and boat to Livingstone Island.
Swim to the pool with guides.

items.name: The Lookout Café
items.summary: A café on the gorge rim, 120 metres above the river, with a view of the bridge.
items.expect: Popular; book for a rail-side table.
items.tip: Come for lunch after the falls walk.
items.why: The best view of any restaurant in town.
flow: Reserve a table by the edge.
Order crocodile kebabs or a burger.

items.name: The Boma – Dinner & Drum Show
items.summary: A buffet dinner of game meats with drumming and dancing.
items.expect: Touristy, lively and fixed-price.
items.tip: Try the warthog and, if you dare, a mopane worm.
items.why: A fun introduction to Zimbabwean food and music.
flow: Reserve and arrive for the welcome.
Eat from the grill and join the drumming.

items.name: Stanley's Terrace, Victoria Falls Hotel
items.summary: Afternoon tea on the lawn terrace of a 1904 hotel, facing the bridge and the spray.
items.expect: A formal, colonial-era setting.
items.tip: Book high tea for 3 pm.
items.why: A piece of history with a view of the gorge.
flow: Walk in through the hotel.
Order high tea for two.

name: Bogotá
tagline: A high-altitude capital of gold and street art
summary: At 2,640 metres, take the first day slowly. See La Candelaria's museums and murals, ride up Monserrate, and take a day trip to the Salt Cathedral.
seasonNote: Cool all year with frequent afternoon showers; April, May, October and November are wettest.
arrival: Use authorised airport taxis or ride-hailing apps; the centre is 30 to 60 minutes away.
gettingAround: Use ride-hailing apps or the TransMilenio bus system; avoid hailing street taxis at night.
cashTip: Cards are common; carry pesos for markets and small cafés and use ATMs inside banks or malls.
foodTip: Try ajiaco (chicken and potato soup), hot chocolate with cheese, arepas and tropical fruit juices.
buyTip: Coffee from specialty roasters, emeralds only from certified dealers, and woven mochila bags.
baseArea: Chapinero or Zona G; La Candelaria by day

connections.note: Frequent flights; the bus takes about 9 hours.

items.name: Monserrate
items.summary: A church on a 3,152-metre peak above the city, reached by funicular or cable car.
items.expect: Thin air; queues at weekends when pilgrims visit.
items.tip: Go on a clear weekday afternoon and stay for sunset.
items.why: The whole of Bogotá spreads out below.
flow: Ride up from the base station.
Walk the terraces and market stalls.
items.best: Late afternoon on a clear day

items.name: Gold Museum
items.summary: More than 30,000 pre-Hispanic gold objects, shown in dramatic dark galleries.
items.expect: Closed on Mondays; free on Sundays and crowded.
items.tip: Save the Offering Room on the top floor for last.
items.why: The largest collection of pre-Columbian gold in the world.
flow: Start on the second floor.
End in the circular Offering Room.

items.name: La Candelaria and Plaza de Bolívar
items.summary: The colonial old town of coloured houses, murals and the grand main square.
items.expect: Lively by day; take a taxi after dark.
items.tip: Join a street art walking tour that starts mid-morning.
items.why: The historic heart of the city and of Colombia's street art scene.
flow: Start at Plaza de Bolívar.
Walk up to Chorro de Quevedo square.

items.name: Botero Museum
items.summary: A free museum of Fernando Botero's rounded figures, plus his collection of Picasso, Monet and Dalí.
items.expect: Closed on Tuesdays.
items.tip: Combine it with the mint museum in the same complex.
items.why: Colombia's most famous artist, in a lovely colonial house.
flow: Walk the Botero rooms.
See his international collection upstairs.

items.name: Salt Cathedral of Zipaquirá
items.summary: A cathedral carved 180 metres underground inside a salt mine, 50 km north of the city.
items.expect: Cool and dim, with a long walk underground.
items.tip: Go on a weekday; Sundays are busy with worshippers.
items.why: A unique feat of mining and faith.
flow: Travel about 90 minutes north.
Walk the Stations of the Cross to the main nave.

items.name: Usaquén Sunday market
items.summary: A former village in the north with a Sunday craft market and good restaurants.
items.expect: Sunday only for the market.
items.tip: Come for brunch, then browse.
items.why: The best place for handmade souvenirs.
flow: Walk the stalls around the square.
Stop for coffee in a courtyard café.

items.name: La Puerta Falsa
items.summary: A tiny eatery open since 1816, beside the cathedral.
items.expect: A queue and shared tables.
items.tip: Order the tamal and chocolate completo.
items.why: The oldest restaurant in Bogotá, serving the classic local snack.
flow: Queue for a table upstairs.
Order ajiaco or a tamal with hot chocolate and cheese.

items.name: Paloquemao Market
items.summary: The city's big produce market, with flowers at dawn, exotic fruit and cooked food stalls.
items.expect: Best in the morning; go by taxi.
items.tip: Ask a fruit seller to cut you a tasting of unfamiliar fruit.
items.why: The easiest way to meet Colombia's fruit: lulo, granadilla, pitahaya.
flow: See the flower market first.
Taste fruit, then eat lechona or a tamal.

items.name: Andrés Carne de Res
items.summary: A vast, surreal steakhouse and dance hall decorated with thousands of handmade objects.
items.expect: A 45-minute drive; it becomes a party late at night.
items.tip: Go on a Saturday and arrange transport back; the city branch (Andrés DC) is easier.
items.why: A one-of-a-kind Colombian night out.
flow: Reserve and arrive by 7 pm.
Eat grilled meats, then stay to dance.

name: Galápagos · Santa Cruz
tagline: Wildlife that isn't afraid of you
summary: Base in Puerto Ayora on Santa Cruz and combine free local walks with day boats to nearby islands. It is costly and tightly regulated, so book boats ahead and follow the two-metre rule with animals.
seasonNote: December to May is warm with calm seas; June to November is cooler and choppier but richest for marine life.
arrival: Fly from Quito or Guayaquil to Baltra, then bus, ferry and road to Puerto Ayora (about 90 minutes). Pay the park fee and transit card in cash.
gettingAround: Walk or use the white pickup taxis in town; water taxis and public speedboats link the islands.
cashTip: Bring US dollars in cash; ATMs are few and can run out.
foodTip: Try ceviche, encocado (fish in coconut sauce) and grilled brujo (scorpionfish) on the kiosk street.
buyTip: Locally made crafts and coffee; never buy coral, shells or lava souvenirs.

connections.note: Usually with a stop in Guayaquil; add the Baltra transfer.

costNote: National park entry (USD 200 for most foreign adults) and day boats (USD 150 to 300 each) are extra.

items.name: Tortuga Bay
items.summary: A long white beach with marine iguanas, and a sheltered lagoon for swimming and kayaking.
items.expect: A 2.5 km paved walk each way; no shade or shops.
items.tip: Swim only in the calm lagoon (Playa Mansa), not on the surf beach.
items.why: The best free beach in the islands.
flow: Sign in at the trailhead.
Walk Playa Brava to the lagoon.

items.name: Charles Darwin Research Station
items.summary: A giant tortoise breeding centre and exhibition, a short walk from town.
items.expect: Guided access to some areas.
items.tip: Go early when the tortoises are fed and active.
items.why: It explains the conservation work that keeps the islands alive.
flow: Walk east from town.
See the hatchlings and adult tortoises.

items.name: El Chato Tortoise Reserve
items.summary: A highland ranch where wild giant tortoises roam freely, with lava tunnels to walk through.
items.expect: Muddy; boots are lent.
items.tip: Combine it with the Los Gemelos craters on the same taxi trip.
items.why: The best place to see giant tortoises in the wild.
flow: Taxi to the highlands.
Walk among the tortoises and through a lava tube.

items.name: Las Grietas
items.summary: A deep crevice between lava cliffs filled with clear, brackish water for swimming.
items.expect: A guide is now required; rocky underfoot.
items.tip: Take a water taxi across and go early.
items.why: A dramatic, cool swimming hole.
flow: Water taxi to the far dock.
Walk 20 minutes past salt ponds and swim.

items.name: Day boat to North Seymour or Bartolomé
items.summary: A guided day trip to an uninhabited island for frigatebirds, blue-footed boobies and snorkelling.
items.expect: Expensive, with limited seats.
items.tip: Book weeks ahead in high season; last-minute deals exist in town.
items.why: The wildlife encounters the Galápagos are famous for.
flow: Bus to the Itabaca Channel and board.
Guided walk, then snorkel with sea lions.

items.name: Puerto Ayora fish market
items.summary: A tiny dockside fish market where pelicans and sea lions queue beside the fishmongers.
items.expect: A five-minute stop.
items.tip: Come when the boats land, late morning or late afternoon.
items.why: The most entertaining free show in town.
flow: Walk along Avenida Charles Darwin.
Watch the animals beg for scraps.

items.name: Los Kioskos
items.summary: A street that fills each evening with tables and grills cooking the day's catch.
items.expect: Simple, busy and good value by island standards.
items.tip: Pick your fish or lobster from the display and agree the price first.
items.why: The best-value seafood dinner in the Galápagos.
flow: Walk the street after 6 pm.
Choose a fish and how it is cooked.

items.name: Il Giardino
items.summary: A garden restaurant on the main street for seafood, pasta and ice cream.
items.expect: Mid-range island prices.
items.tip: Good for a relaxed lunch out of the sun.
items.why: A reliable, comfortable choice on the waterfront road.
flow: Take a table in the garden.
Order ceviche or tuna.

items.name: 1835 Coffee Lab
items.summary: A small café roasting coffee grown in the Galápagos highlands.
items.expect: A few seats.
items.tip: Buy a bag of island beans to take home.
items.why: Galápagos coffee is rare and grown in volcanic soil.
flow: Order at the bar.
Try a pour-over of island coffee.
